note: Parses the uSWID header from attacker-controlled input; header contains magic, hdrver, hdrsz, payloadsz, flags, compression.
Extracts the header version from the parsed header; must be >= 1 to proceed.
Extracts header size and payload size from the attacker-controlled header; payloadsz must be non-zero.
For hdrver >= 2, compression is determined from the flags field; attacker controls this.

code: payload = fu_input_stream_read_bytes(stream, offset + hdrsz, payloadsz, error);
note: Reads the payload bytes from the input stream at offset+hdrsz with length payloadsz; this is the attacker-controlled CBOR data.
Updates payloadsz to the actual decompressed/read payload size.
Iterates over the payload, parsing each coSWID CBOR section sequentially.

code: fw2 = fu_bytes_new_offset(payload, offset_tmp, payloadsz - offset_tmp, error);
note: Creates a GBytes slice of the remaining payload starting at offset_tmp.

code: if (!fu_firmware_parse(firmware_coswid, fw2, flags | FWUPD_INSTALL_FLAG_NO_SEARCH, error)) return FALSE;
note: Parses the CBOR slice as a coSWID firmware; this invokes fu_coswid_firmware_parse on the attacker-controlled CBOR data.
Loads the CBOR data using libcbor; the result is a cbor_item_t tree built from attacker-controlled bytes.
Gets the map pairs from the root CBOR item; attacker controls the map structure.
Reads the tag ID from each map key; attacker controls which tags are present.

code: if (!fu_coswid_firmware_parse_one_or_many(self, pairs[i].value, fu_coswid_firmware_parse_entity, NULL, error)) return FALSE;
note: When tag_id is FU_COSWID_TAG_ENTITY, dispatches the value to fu_coswid_firmware_parse_entity; attacker controls the entity map.
Gets the map pairs from the entity CBOR item; attacker controls the entity structure.
Reads the tag ID from each entity map key; attacker controls which tags are present.

code: if (cbor_isa_uint(pairs[i].value)) { FuCoswidEntityRole role = cbor_get_uint8(pairs[i].value); entity->roles[entity_role_cnt++] = role; }
note: When the ROLE tag value is a uint, writes to entity->roles[entity_role_cnt++] WITHOUT checking if entity_role_cnt >= 6; if entity_role_cnt is already 6, this writes out of bounds of the 6-element roles array, causing a heap-buffer-overflow.

After the uint case, the code still enters the for loop and calls cbor_array_size on the same non-array item; in libcbor this reads from the item's data union which may be uninitialized or out of bounds, leading to a heap-buffer-overflow READ 8.

Reads 8 bytes from the array element via cbor_get_uint8; if the array size from the previous step was corrupted or the element is not a valid uint, this reads out of bounds, triggering the heap-buffer-overflow READ 8.
